intro: School and university words, with several false friends of English.
p.carrera.consejo: Here it means university studies, not a competition. «Estudio la carrera de Medicina» is very normal.
p.asignatura.consejo: Do not say «sujeto»: a school subject is an «asignatura». «Sujeto» is the subject of a sentence.
p.aprobar.consejo: The o becomes ue: «apruebo», «aprueba», but «aprobamos». Its opposite is «suspender».
p.suspender.consejo: With an exam it is not «to suspend»: it means to fail. The bad mark is called «suspenso».
p.nota.consejo: The verb for getting a mark is «sacar»: «saco un ocho». In Spain marks go from 0 to 10, and a five is a pass.
p.beca.consejo: You ask for a beca with «pedir» or get one with «conseguir». A «beca de estudios» helps to pay for university.
p.matricularse.consejo: It goes with «en»: «me matriculo en Historia». It is a verb with «se», like «levantarse».
p.instituto.consejo: In Spain, after primary school you go to the «instituto». There you do the ESO and, if you want, the bachillerato.
p.máster.consejo: It has an accent: MÁS-ter. The plural is «másteres». It is usually done after the degree.
p.apuntes.consejo: It is almost always plural: «tomar apuntes» in class and «repasar los apuntes» at home.
p.repasar.consejo: It starts with «re-», which means «again»: you study again what you already saw.
p.examen.consejo: The x sounds «ks»: ek-SA-men. The plural takes an accent, «exámenes», but the strong syllable is the same.
p.prácticas.consejo: In this sense it is plural: «hacer prácticas» is working as a student in a company.
b1.titulo: The school system and its false friends
b1.texto:
In Spain you study at **el colegio** (primary school) and then at **el instituto**: the ESO runs from age 12 to 16 and the **bachillerato**, optional, from 16 to 18. At university you do **un grado** and then you can go on with **un máster** or **un doctorado**.

Marks go from 0 to 10: below 5 is **suspenso**; **aprobado** is 5 to 6.9; **notable**, 7 to 8.9; and **sobresaliente**, 9 to 10.

Watch out for false friends:

- **carrera** means university studies (and also a sports race).
- **colegio** is a school, not a «college».
- **asignatura** is a school subject; **sujeto** is the subject of a sentence.
- **suspender** an exam means to fail it.
b2.f1.texto: I have passed everything, but I have failed Statistics.
b2.f2.texto: What mark did you get in History?
b2.f4.texto: If you keep getting good marks, they will give you a scholarship.
b2.f5.texto: When I finish my degree, I want to do a master's.
b2.f6.texto: I prefer to do a work placement in a company.
b4.texto:
To talk about the future with conditions, two formulas are very useful:

- **Si** + present → future: **Si estudias, aprobarás**. It is a possible condition.
- **Cuando** + subjunctive → future: **Cuando termine la carrera, haré un máster**. If the moment has not arrived yet, the verb after «cuando» is subjunctive.

With habits, «cuando» takes the ordinary present: **Cuando estudio, apago el móvil**.

For what has just happened use the present perfect (**he** + participle): **He suspendido Estadística**. The participle of **aprobar** is **aprobado** and of **sacar**, **sacado**.
b4.e0.texto: If you study every day, you will pass all the subjects.
b4.e1.texto: When I finish my degree, I will look for a job.
b4.e2.texto: This week I have revised all my notes.
b5.f0.texto: The university library smells of old paper and coffee.
b5.f1.texto: Through the high windows comes a white winter light.
b5.f2.texto: Pablo takes a table at the back and opens his notes with cold hands.
b5.f3.texto: Every page has blue arrows and underlined sentences.
b5.f4.texto: A clock slowly marks the hours left before the exam.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía arrives with two coffees and sits down opposite him.
b5.f6.texto: Pablo looks up and smiles with tiredness.
b5.f7.texto: Outside, the students cross the yard with their bags over their shoulders.
b5.f8.texto: A cold wind moves the dry leaves of the trees.
b5.f9.texto: Pablo closes his notes, takes a sip of coffee and breathes deeply.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That is it! «Suspender» means to fail, not «to suspend».
b6.o1.refuerzo: A ten is the top mark. «Suspender» is the opposite.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Matricularse» is signing up for a course. «Suspender» is failing.
b7.frase: Cuando ____ la carrera, haré un máster.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! The moment has not come yet: «cuando» takes the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Termino» works for habits, not for a future plan.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The future tense is not used after «cuando» when you talk about the future.
b7.pregunta: You talk about the future. Which verb goes after «cuando»?
b8.frase: Si estudias mucho aprobarás el examen
b8.traduccion: If you study a lot you will pass the exam
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is another meaning of «carrera», but it does not fit with Medicine.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The timetable is a chart of hours, not a «carrera».
b9.pregunta: I study the carrera of Medicine. What is «carrera»?
b10.frase: Pablo ha ____ un nueve en Historia.
b10.o0.refuerzo: You say «hacer un examen», but not «hacer una nota».
b10.o1.refuerzo: You take notes («tomar apuntes»), but you get marks («sacar notas»).
b10.o2.refuerzo: That is it! The verb for marks is «sacar»: «sacar un nueve».
b10.pregunta: Which verb is used with a mark?
b12.o2.refuerzo: That happens after an exam, not when you enrol.
b12.pregunta: What do you do when you «te matriculas»?
p.suspendido.consejo: Participle of «suspender»: «he suspendido» means I failed.
p.sigues.consejo: With a gerund it means to keep doing: «sigues sacando».
p.notas.consejo: Plural of «nota». «Buenas notas» means good marks.
p.darán.consejo: Future of «dar»: «darán» has an accent on the last syllable.
p.termine.consejo: Subjunctive of «terminar». It goes after «cuando» for the future.
p.estudias.consejo: Present of «estudiar» for «tú». «Si estudias» is a possible condition.
p.aprobarás.consejo: Future of «aprobar». It is regular: the o does not change.
p.asignaturas.consejo: Plural of «asignatura». «Todas las asignaturas» means all subjects.
p.buscaré.consejo: Future of «buscar». The accent marks the stress on the last syllable.
p.repasado.consejo: Participle of «repasar»: «he repasado» is the present perfect.
p.altas.consejo: Feminine plural of «alto». It agrees with «ventanas».
p.flechas.consejo: Plural of «flecha». The «ch» sounds like in «chocolate».
p.subrayadas.consejo: Participle of «subrayar», used as an adjective: «frases subrayadas».
p.faltan.consejo: «Faltan horas» means there are hours left until something.
p.cafés.consejo: Plural of «café». It keeps the accent: «cafés».
p.toma.consejo: «Tomar un sorbo» means to take a sip. It also means to drink.
p.sorbo.consejo: Said with «tomar» or «beber»: «un sorbo de café».
p.superado.consejo: Participle of «superar». «Superar una asignatura» is to pass it.
p.estudios.consejo: Plural of «estudio». «Los estudios» are your education.
p.apuntas.consejo: «Te apuntas a un curso» means you register for a course.
